Control Accounts — Suppliers

Control accounts for suppliers are summary accounts that automatically consolidate all amounts owed to suppliers into a single balance sheet account.

Use this screen to manage how supplier balances are grouped and displayed in your financial reports.

Name
Name

The name identifies this control account in your general ledger and financial reports.

Understanding Control Accounts

Control accounts are summary accounts in the general ledger that represent the total of all individual supplier balances. They automatically consolidate amounts owed to suppliers, providing a comprehensive view of your accounts payable.

The system automatically updates the control account balance whenever you create or modify transactions involving suppliers. This ensures your general ledger always reflects the total of detailed supplier records without manual reconciliation.

Naming Your Control Accounts

Choose clear, descriptive names that identify the type of suppliers or payables being tracked. Common examples include:

• Trade Payables - For regular inventory and material suppliers

• Accrued Expenses - For services received but not yet invoiced

• Vendor Deposits - For advance payments to suppliers

Best Practices

Consider creating separate control accounts for different supplier categories to improve cash flow management and financial analysis. For example:

• Group inventory suppliers separately from service providers

• Separate current payables from overdue amounts

• Distinguish between domestic and foreign suppliers if you deal in multiple currencies

Group
Group

Select the balance sheet group where this control account should appear in financial reports. This determines how supplier balances are categorized on your balance sheet.
